stem: In a certain code, each letter is replaced by its position number in the reverse alphabet (A = 26, B = 25, C = 24, ..., Z = 1). Using this rule, what is the code for the word CALM?

per_option_rationale.rationale: C=24, A=26, L=15, M=14 by the rule reverse position = 26 - (forward position - 1) = 27 - position. C is 3rd so 27-3=24; A is 1st so 27-1=26; L is 12th so 27-12=15; M is 13th so 27-13=14.
31 for C arises from adding 28 instead of subtracting from 27, a misapplication of the reversal formula producing an out-of-range value.
12 for L and 13 for M are the forward-alphabet positions (L=12, M=13), not the reverse positions, meaning the student forgot to subtract from 27.
12 for L is the forward position; 15 for M uses the reverse rule for L by mistake, swapping the computations for L and M.

explanation: Reverse-alphabet position = 27 - forward position. C(3)->24, A(1)->26, L(12)->15, M(13)->14. Code: 24 26 15 14.

explanation_sections.punchline: The reversal formula is 27 minus the standard alphabetical position of each letter.
explanation_sections.approach: Deductive trace: identify the coding rule (reverse position = 27 - standard position), apply it letter by letter in order: C->24, A->26, L->15, M->14, and concatenate.
explanation_sections.lesson: Always verify with the anchor letters: A maps to 26 and Z maps to 1 under a full reversal.
explanation_sections.timing: 45 seconds. The main trap is using forward positions (L=12, M=13) instead of reverse positions.
